title: Essence Drain Contagion Lich — 0.5.4 Research Draft
summary: A source-linked Chaos DoT draft that separates pack spreading, boss upkeep and Full-Life or Low-Life endgame decisions.
description: Research draft for a Path of Exile 2 Essence Drain and Contagion Lich build on the 0.5.4 baseline.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: A Lich spreading violet Essence Drain and Contagion through a dark enemy pack

sections.title: Build Overview
paragraphs: ED + Contagion is effective because it turns target selection into propagation: Contagion marks the pack, Essence Drain supplies the damaging debuff, and a death carries the package onward. The build feels poor when those two casts land on unrelated targets, so aiming and pack order matter more than another line of tooltip damage.

For bosses, propagation disappears. The build becomes a maintenance setup: keep Essence Drain active, add Despair only when the target warrants the cast, maintain Dark Effigy totems, and move while damage over time continues. That mobility is the payoff for accepting a slower, layered damage ramp.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Low gear floor for campaign progression.
Damage continues while the player repositions.
Contagion can turn one successful application into pack clear.
cons: Damage is delayed rather than immediate.
Bossing needs several debuffs or auxiliary skills.
Different endgame guides disagree on auxiliary skills and defence.

sections.title: Mapping
paragraphs: Cast Contagion into the center of a connected pack, then land Essence Drain on a target inside it. Move immediately and watch whether the debuff propagates before spending another cast. Unearth or the minion layer can bridge awkward remains, but should not replace correct targeting.
Tag a dense pack, confirm the spread starts, then move ahead. If propagation fails, check skill order, range, duration and whether the first target died with both effects.

sections.title: Bossing
paragraphs: Use Contagion only if it contributes to the chosen setup, maintain Essence Drain, add Despair, and keep the allowed Dark Effigy count active. The correct rhythm is refresh → reposition → refresh, not continuous stationary casting.
Maintain Essence Drain, Despair and the selected auxiliary debuff while moving. Dark Effigy, Entangle or Bonestorm are variant choices until their exact role is verified.

items.question: Why does one pack disappear and the next barely moves?
answer: The successful pack likely received Contagion and Essence Drain on the same connected group. In the failed pack, ED may have hit outside the Contagion set or the monsters were too separated to propagate.
bullets: Aim Contagion at the pack center.
Wait long enough to observe the first spread.
Use terrain to group monsters before recasting.

items.question: Should I use Entangle instead?
answer: Use it if you value simpler targeting. Community discussion treats it as a quality-of-life alternative, not proof that ED + Contagion is invalid. The trade is a different clear pattern and support package.

items.question: What if I want a more immediate caster?
answer: The cold Chronomancer route has a more direct hit-and-freeze rhythm, but requires a staged gem swap and closer positioning.

entries.label: 0.5 ED + Contagion experience thread
entries.statement: Players report that the pair can progress on several ascendancies and feels easy early, while one responder prefers Entangle because it removes the need to aim ED and manage Unearth spreading.
entries.context: This explains why the build can be strong yet still feel awkward to a player who dislikes two-step targeting.

entries.label: Ronarray ED + Contagion Lich guide
entries.statement: The maintained guide uses Contagion then Essence Drain for packs, adds Despair only when required, and keeps Dark Effigy totems active for bosses while the player moves.
entries.context: That sequence is used here as a rotation model, not copied as a claim that every listed item is mandatory.
